Speed Limit Review - 
update 
The Department of Transport carried out a Review of 
Speed Limits nationally and this has resulted in changes 
to the default speed limits for roads in Ireland. These 
changes were signed into law in April 2024.   The 
changes to the legislation will reduce the default speed 
limits on some road categories including:  
 
• 
60km/hr on Rural Local Roads (reduction 
from 80km/hr) 
• 
80km/hr on National Secondary Roads 
(currently 100km/hr) 
• 
30km/hr in Urban Areas (currently 
predominantly 50km/hr). 
 
The implementation of the reduction of a default speed 
limit on Rural Local Roads to 60km/hr is complete.   
 
It is proposed by the National 
Group that implementation of the 
speed limits will be done in phases:  
• 
Phase 1 - Complete 
• 
Phase 2 - Urban Areas  
• 
Phase 3 - Other Special 
Circumstances, schools etc.   
 
Progress on Phase 2 has 
commenced with pre-consultation 
letters issued. Districts are currently 
reviewing urban areas within their 
operational areas.  
 
Initial Workshops with Members 
are being confirmed with the 
District Administrators.

CFRAM FLOOD RELIEF SCHEMES 
Flood Relief Schemes 
Current Update 
Ballina FRS 
The first consultation with the public and stakeholders took 
place online from 8th November – 6th December 2021. The 
second public consultation day was held 12th June 2025 during 
which the community were presented with five options 
developed to alleviate flooding including the emerging preferred 
option.  
Significant requests for further information and amendments to 
the scheme were made by attendees.  The design team are 
currently undertaking a high-level review taking these 
submissions into consideration.  
Upon selection of the emerging preferred option, the scheme 
would then proceed to Stage II, the planning process, where the 
preferred option would be developed and an application 
submitted to An Coimisiún Pleanála. 
Golden FRS 
The Golden FRS failed the Scheme Viability Review Report 
(SVR) which concluded that there is no potentially economical 
scheme that could be taken to full Flood Relief Scheme project 
stage. 
Tipperary County Council requested that the OPW reconsider 
this decision and allow the Golden Scheme to advance to Stage 
1 Option Selection. This would enable a more detailed analysis 
of the available options and provide greater certainty regarding 
the associated cost estimates.  
Holycross FRS 
Stage 1 Option Selection for Holycross FRS is complete. The 
proposed Capital Flood Relief Scheme was not accepted by the 
benefitting property owners. 
 
Knocklofty FRS 
In July 2024 the OPW approved the Preferred Option in the 
Options Report, which enabled progression of the Knocklofty 
FRS.  The Preferred Option is to construct raised defences on 
the River Suir to prevent flooding with stormwater drainage 
behind the defences. Total budget of €1.1m.  
This option was presented to the public for feedback on 17th 
April 2025 during the second Public Consultation Day for the 
scheme. The scheme received largely positive feedback and 
issues raised by the public have been taken into consideration.  
This project is currently in Stage II, the planning process, where 
the preferred option is being developed and an application will 
be submitted to An Coimisiún Pleanála in 2026.

Flood Relief Schemes 
Current Update 
Marlfield Lake FRS 
The ground investigation for the scheme was completed in 
January 2026 and samples taken during this have been sent for 
laboratory testing. The results will facilitate the Design Team in 
selecting the most appropriate design options for the Marlfield 
Flood Relief Scheme. Upon selection of the emerging preferred 
option, the scheme would then proceed to Stage II, the planning 
process, where the preferred option would be developed and an 
application submitted to An Coimisiún Pleanála. 
In parallel with the Capital FRS in Marlfield, work is continuing 
with the interim dam rehabilitation protection works involving 
various interim measures that will protect the existing dam and 
the surrounding area. Undertaking work in Marlfield Lake area 
is complex with many environmental and statutory constraints, 
however we have been engaging with the relevant stakeholders 
and significant progress has been made. 
All of the above is subject to OPW funding and approval. 
Nenagh FRS 
The scope and complexity of the Nenagh Flood Relief Scheme 
have evolved significantly, and the scheme was formally 
reclassified in September 2023 from a ‘small project’ to a major 
flood relief scheme.  This decision reflects the scale of works 
required, the inclusion of critical infrastructure, and the need for 
robust governance and resources for a capital project of such 
magnitude. 
Preparatory work by the OPW has been ongoing with 
preliminary site surveys (topographical and CCTV) completed in 
Q4 2025.  
A Steering Group has been established to oversee delivery of the 
Nenagh FRS. 
Tender documents for the procurement of consultants to 
progress both the engineering and environmental elements of 
the scheme are currently being prepared. 
Stage I – Option Identification & Preliminary Design will 
commence following the procurement and appointment of the 
Design Team.  This is expected to progress in 2026 subject to 
OPW approval.

Digital Transformation – Roads Operational Management 
  
The Roads Directorate progress on the digital transformation of operations and asset management through the 
rollout of the ProWork software continues.  One to one training is ongoing with GSS’s and relevant staff.  The 
system manages and records: 
 
• 
Job details linked to the Safety Management System (SMS) Tasks 
• 
TTMP – Temporary Traffic Management Plans 
• 
SSWP – Safe System of Work Plan - linked to SMS Tasks 
• 
TBT – Tool Box Talks - delivery and record management 
• 
Staff Department and Area 
• 
Staff PPE management (Thurles commencing pilot) 
• 
Staff Training management (School Wardens, CPC and National Licences currently transferring to 
system) 
• 
Equipment management and service record 
• 
Plant and Vehicle Management and service record 
• 
Asset Inspection and action management 
• 
HSQA Inspection and action management.  
 
The system will allow review of operations, reduce administrative time, delivery of safety information, activity 
review and ease of audit for our Safety Management System and ISO 45001. It will also identify opportunities 
for efficiencies and improvements. The project is ongoing in 2026 and is integrated into the sections Safety 
Management System.
